docs.title: formance2blnk
docs.text:
Migrate a Formance Ledger into Blnk — safely, resumably and verifiably.

formance2blnk reads transactions and balances from the Formance Ledger v2 API and records them in Blnk. It ships as a single static CLI and as a dependency-free Go library you can embed in your own tooling.

  • Why formance2blnk — the fiat/crypto separation that motivated this tool.
  • Getting started — install and run your first migration in minutes.
  • Strategies — replay, snapshot or hybrid: pick what your audit needs.
  • Mapping — route Formance addresses to Blnk ledgers and indicators.
  • Reconciliation — prove the two ledgers agree before you cut over.

docs.title: Why it's safe to run
docs.text: Guarantee How No double-posting Every Blnk transaction has a deterministic reference (fm:<ledger>:<txid>:<posting>, or fm-open:<ledger>:<address>:<asset> for opening balances). Blnk rejects duplicates, and the migrator treats a duplicate as "already done". Resumable The last fully written Formance transaction is checkpointed in a locked state file. Ctrl-C, a crash or a deploy — just run the same command again. Atomic transactions All postings of a Formance transaction are written in one atomic Blnk bulk call (as long as they fit in batch_size, max 50). Exact amounts Amounts are arbitrary-precision integers from end to end; never floats. Ordered Transactions are applied strictly in Formance ID order, with skip_queue so Blnk applies them synchronously. Verifiable reconcile compares every balance — and optionally credit/debit volumes — and exits with code 2 on any difference.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Formance
    T[Transactions v2] --> R
    V[Volumes v2] --> S
  end
  R[Replay] --> M{{Mapper}}
  S[Snapshot] --> M
  M -->|balance IDs / @indicators| W[Atomic bulk writer]
  W --> B[(Blnk)]
  W <--> ST[(State file<br/>checkpoints + IDs)]
  B --> RC[Reconcile]
  V --> RC

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
formance2blnk init > formance2blnk.json   # write a starter config
formance2blnk plan                         # dry run
formance2blnk migrate                      # run (resumable)
formance2blnk reconcile -volumes           # verify

Not affiliated

formance2blnk is an independent open-source project, released under the MIT license. It is not affiliated with Formance or Blnk Finance.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Replay, snapshot and hybrid migration strategies.
  • Rule-based account mapping (ledgers, indicators, skip) with templates, and a pluggable Mapper interface.
  • Asset translation (USD/2 → USD / precision 100) with overrides.
  • Deterministic references, checkpointing and a locked JSON state file for safe resumption.
  • Atomic bulk writes with duplicate-reference recovery.
  • Reconciliation of balances and credit/debit volumes with text, JSON and CSV reports.
  • Formance client with bearer and OAuth2 client-credentials auth; descending-order fallback.
  • JSON configuration with ${ENV} / ${ENV:-default} expansion and secret redaction.
  • CLI: init, validate, plan, migrate, reconcile, version, help.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
formance2blnk <command> [flags]
Command Description init Print a starter configuration to stdout. validate Check the configuration and print it with secrets redacted. plan Dry run of the configured mode. Reads Formance, writes nothing. migrate Run the migration. Resumable and safe to re-run. reconcile Compare Formance and Blnk. Exit code 2 on mismatch. version Print version, commit and build date. Also -version, --version. help Print usage. Also -h, --help. Running with no command prints usage to stderr and exits 64.

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text:
validate, plan, migrate and reconcile accept every flag below (run formance2blnk <command> -h to list them); a flag only has an effect where documented. -mode, -cutoff and -state are applied before validation, so they also affect validate.

Flag Default Description -config path formance2blnk.json Configuration file. -state path from config Override state_file. -log-level level info debug, info, warn, error. -log-format fmt text text or json (for log shipping).

docs.title: plan and migrate
docs.text:
Flag Description -mode m Override migration.mode: replay, snapshot or hybrid. -cutoff t Override migration.cutoff (RFC 3339) for hybrid mode. -json Print the summary as JSON.

The summary title is the phase (replay, snapshot or hybrid), suffixed with (plan) for plan, which also ends with plan only: nothing was written to Blnk or the state file. Example summary:

replay summary
  Formance transactions read   125034
  Blnk transactions written    188211
  Already migrated (skipped)   0
  Blnk ledgers created         3
  Blnk balances created        40112
  Skipped: zero_amount         4
  Checkpoint main              tx 125033
  Elapsed                      41m12.4s

Skip reasons: before_cutoff, reverted, revert, zero_amount, self_posting, same_endpoint, skipped_account, transform, world, zero_balance.

docs.title: reconcile
docs.text: Flag Default Description -volumes false Also compare credit/debit volumes (after a full replay). -skip-indicators false Ignore @indicator balances. -format f text text, json or csv. -out file stdout Write the report to a file; a one-line summary is still printed to stdout. -workers n 8 Concurrent Blnk balance lookups.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Success 1 Error, including an invalid configuration and interruption (progress is saved) 2 Reconciliation mismatch 64 Usage error: no or unknown command, bad flag, invalid -log-level or -log-format

docs.title: Signals
docs.text: SIGINT (Ctrl-C) and SIGTERM stop the run gracefully: in-flight requests are cancelled, the state file is flushed and unlocked. Re-run the same command to resume.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text: formance2blnk targets the Formance Ledger v2 REST API and the Blnk Core API. It uses a deliberately small surface of each, listed below, so you can check it against the versions you run.

docs.title: Formance (read-only)
docs.text:
Endpoint Used for GET /v2 (library) listing ledgers GET /v2/{ledger}/transactions Replay — cursor pagination, pageSize, reverse=true GET /v2/{ledger}/transactions/{id} (library) formance.Client.GetTransaction GET /v2/{ledger}/volumes Snapshot (with endTime) and reconciliation; insertionDate=true is available to library users GET /v2/{ledger}/accounts/{address} copy_account_metadata POST /api/auth/oauth/token OAuth2 client credentials (Formance Cloud / secured stacks). Resolved against the origin of formance.url; override with token_url.

Assumptions:

  • Responses use the v2 cursor envelope: {"cursor": {"hasMore", "next", "data": [...]}}; single objects are wrapped in {"data": ...}.
  • When cursor is set, no other query parameters are sent (Formance rejects them).
  • Transaction IDs and amounts may be JSON numbers or strings and may exceed 64-bit floats; both are decoded exactly.
  • Reverts are identified by the com.formance.spec/state/reverts metadata key, reverted originals by the reverted field.
  • If reverse=true is not honoured, the client detects newest-first order and falls back to buffering. You can set another query string with ascending_params.

docs.title: Blnk (write)
docs.text:
Endpoint Used for POST /ledgers Creating ledgers POST /balances Creating balances GET /balances/{id} Reconciling balances GET /balances/indicator/{indicator}/currency/{currency} Reconciling indicator balances (404 counts as zero) POST /transactions Writes that contain exactly one transaction (always the case with batch_size: 1) POST /transactions/bulk Atomic batches (atomic: true, run_async: false, skip_queue: true)

Assumptions:

  • Authentication is the X-Blnk-Key header (omitted when api_key is empty).
  • Amounts are sent as precise_amount (integer minor units) with precision.
  • A duplicate reference is reported as a 400/409/422 error whose message mentions the reference being already used / existing. This is how resumed runs recognise already-migrated data. If your Blnk version words it differently, blnk.IsDuplicateReference is the single place to adjust.
  • Atomic bulk batches are limited to 50 transactions. A Formance transaction with more postings than batch_size is written in several calls and is therefore not atomic (a warning is logged).
  • Requests are retried on network errors, 429 and 5xx responses with backoff. If a write succeeded but its response was lost, the retry is recognised as a duplicate reference.

docs.title: Supported Go versions
docs.text:
Go 1.22 and the latest stable release are tested in CI.

Verify before production

APIs evolve. Before a production migration, run plan, then a full migrate + reconcile -volumes against staging copies of both systems. The reconciliation is independent of these assumptions: if it passes, the data matches.

docs.title: Data model mapping
docs.text:
Both systems are double-entry ledgers that store money as integers in minor units, so the models map closely.

Formance Blnk Notes Ledger Ledger Name taken from mapping rules (default: same name). Account address (users:42:wallet) Balance One Blnk balance per account per asset — Blnk balances are single-currency. world @World An internal (indicator) balance Blnk creates on first use. Configurable. Asset USD/2 Currency USD, precision 100 The number after / is the number of decimals. Posting Transaction precise_amount carries the exact integer. Transaction with N postings N transactions in one atomic bulk call All-or-nothing. timestamp effective_date Preserves backdating. Transaction metadata meta_data.formance_metadata Plus provenance keys, see below. Account metadata Balance meta_data.formance_metadata With copy_account_metadata: true. Revert A reversal transaction Or drop both with reverts: skip.

docs.text:
Every migrated object carries enough information to trace it back:

TransactionBalanceOpening balance

  "formance_posting": 0,
  "formance_source": "users:1:wallet",
  "formance_destination": "platform:fees",
  "formance_asset": "USD/2",
  "formance_reference": "order-889",
  "formance_metadata": { "order_id": "889" }
}

{
  "formance_ledger": "main",
  "formance_address": "users:1:wallet",
  "formance_asset": "USD/2",
  "migrated_by": "formance2blnk",
  "formance_metadata": { "kyc": "tier2" }
}

{
  "formance_ledger": "main",
  "formance_address": "users:1:wallet",
  "formance_asset": "USD/2",
  "formance_input": "5000",
  "formance_output": "1250",
  "opening_balance": true,
  "as_of": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}

as_of is only present for SnapshotAsOf and hybrid runs.

docs.title: References and idempotency
docs.text:
Blnk requires a unique reference per transaction and refuses duplicates. formance2blnk builds references deterministically:

Kind Format Example Replayed posting <prefix>:<ledger>:<txid>:<posting> fm:main:1042:0 Opening balance <prefix>-open:<ledger>:<address>:<asset> fm-open:main:users:1:wallet:USD/2

The prefix defaults to fm (reference_prefix). Because a reference identifies its source posting, re-sending the same posting can never create a second transaction. When a write fails because the reference already exists, the migrator counts it as already migrated and continues.

docs.title: Checkpoints and the state file
docs.text:
The state file (state_file, default formance2blnk-state.json) records:

  • the Blnk ledger_id created for each ledger name;
  • the Blnk balance_id created for each (Formance ledger, address, asset);
  • per Formance ledger, the last transaction ID whose postings are all durable in Blnk, and whether the snapshot phase completed (with its as-of time, so a hybrid run cannot be resumed with a different cutoff);
  • with reverts: skip, the IDs of reverted transactions that were dropped, so their reverts are dropped too, even in a later run.

Writes are atomic (temp file + fsync + rename + directory fsync) and the file is protected by a .lock file, so two migrators can never share it.

Keep the state file

The state file is how the migrator knows which Blnk balance belongs to which Formance account. Losing it mid-migration does not cause double-posting (references prevent that) but new balances would be created for accounts that already have one. Back it up, and keep it for reconciliation.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text:
Formance transaction IDs are monotonic. The migrator processes them strictly in ascending ID order and writes with skip_queue: true, so Blnk applies each batch synchronously, in order, before the next one is sent. Effective dates are preserved even when Formance transactions were backdated.

The Formance list endpoint returns newest-first by default. The client requests oldest-first (reverse=true, configurable via ascending_params); if the server ignores it, the client detects descending order and buffers — and when resuming, it stops paging as soon as it reaches the checkpoint.

docs.title: Batching and atomicity
docs.text:
Postings are collected into atomic bulk calls of up to batch_size Blnk transactions (Blnk's limit for atomic batches is 50). A Formance transaction is never split across calls unless it alone has more than batch_size postings, in which case it is written in chunks of batch_size and a warning is logged.

If a batch fails because one of its references already exists (typical after a crash between the write and the checkpoint), the migrator retries group by group. If a group with several postings still reports a duplicate, each of its postings is then sent on its own: an earlier run with a smaller batch_size may have written only part of it, and every posting already present is counted as already migrated while the missing ones are written.

docs.title: Overdrafts
docs.text: Formance already validated every historical transaction, and its overdraft rules (Numscript allowing unbounded overdraft, etc.) have no direct Blnk equivalent. Replayed transactions are therefore sent with allow_overdraft: true by default. Set enforce_balances: true if you want Blnk to re-validate funds — expect rejections wherever Formance allowed overdrafts.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
The CLI reads a JSON file (default formance2blnk.json, override with -config). Generate a starter file with formance2blnk init.

Any JSON string value can reference environment variables as ${NAME} or ${NAME:-default}. A variable that is unset or empty expands to its default, or to an empty string if there is none. Numbers and booleans cannot be taken from the environment. Unknown keys are rejected, so typos fail fast.

formance2blnk validate checks the whole file, including batch_size (0–50), reverts, on_skipped_account, asset decimals and the hybrid cutoff, without contacting either server.

{
  "formance": {
    "url": "https://${FORMANCE_ORG}.${FORMANCE_ENV:-eu.sandbox}.formance.cloud/api/ledger",
    "ledgers": ["main"],
    "client_id": "${FORMANCE_CLIENT_ID}",
    "client_secret": "${FORMANCE_CLIENT_SECRET}",
    "scopes": ["ledger:read"],
    "requests_per_second": 20
  },
  "blnk": {
    "url": "${BLNK_URL}",
    "api_key": "${BLNK_API_KEY}",
    "requests_per_second": 50
  },
  "mapping": {
    "world_indicator": "@World",
    "rules": [
      { "match": "platform:fees", "indicator": "@Fees" },
      { "match": "banks:*", "indicator": "@Bank-{1}" },
      { "match": "users:*:wallet", "ledger": "Customer Wallets" },
      { "match": "sandbox:**", "skip": true }
    ],
    "assets": {
      "COIN": { "currency": "NGN", "decimals": 2 }
    }
  },
  "migration": {
    "mode": "hybrid",
    "cutoff": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "reverts": "skip",
    "on_skipped_account": "drop"
  },
  "state_file": "formance2blnk-state/hybrid.json"
}

docs.title: formance
docs.text: Key Type Default Description url string required Ledger API root without /v2. Self-hosted: http://localhost:3068. Formance Cloud: https://ORG.ENV.formance.cloud/api/ledger. ledgers string[] required Formance ledgers to migrate, in order. token string Static bearer token. client_id / client_secret string OAuth2 client-credentials. Mutually exclusive with token. token_url string <origin>/api/auth/oauth/token OAuth2 token endpoint (used with client_id). scopes string[] OAuth2 scopes, e.g. ["ledger:read"]. page_size int 100 Page size for list calls. requests_per_second number unlimited Client-side rate limit. ascending_params string reverse=true Query string that makes the transaction list oldest-first.

docs.title: blnk
docs.text: Key Type Default Description url string required Blnk base URL, e.g. http://localhost:5001. api_key string Sent as X-Blnk-Key. Leave empty for unsecured local instances. requests_per_second number unlimited Client-side rate limit.

docs.title: mapping
docs.text: Key Type Default Description rules rule[] [] Ordered rules; see Mapping. Each rule has match and exactly one of ledger, indicator (must start with @), skip. world_indicator string @World Target for Formance's world account. Must start with @. default_ledger string {ledger} Blnk ledger for unmatched accounts. assets object Per-asset overrides keyed by Formance asset (e.g. USD/2): { "USD/2": { "currency": "...", "decimals": n } } with n between 0 and 30. Both fields are optional.

docs.title: migration
docs.text: Key Type Default Description mode string replay replay, snapshot or hybrid. See Strategies. Override with -mode. cutoff RFC 3339 Required for hybrid; must not be in the future and cannot change once the snapshot completed. Override with -cutoff. reference_prefix string fm Prefix of every Blnk reference. Changing it creates an independent copy. batch_size int 50 Blnk transactions per atomic bulk call (1–50; 0 means the default). Use 1 to send one at a time. enforce_balances bool false Send allow_overdraft: false on replayed transactions. reverts string replay replay or skip. on_skipped_account string error error or drop. copy_account_metadata bool false Copy Formance account metadata onto new Blnk balances (one extra request per account). opening_indicator string world indicator Counter-party of opening balances in snapshot/hybrid. include_zero_balances bool false Snapshot: create balances for zero-balance accounts.

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Key Type Default Description state_file string formance2blnk-state.json Progress and ID store. Missing parent directories are created. Override with -state.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thanks for helping improve formance2blnk!

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
Requirements: Go 1.22+. Optional: golangci-lint, Python 3 for docs (pip install -r docs-src/requirements.txt).

make fmt          # gofmt -s
make check        # vet, lint (if installed), race tests, gofmt check
make cover        # coverage report
make build        # bin/formance2blnk
make docs         # build docs-src/ into docs/ (commit the result)
make docs-serve   # live docs at http://127.0.0.1:8000
go run ./examples/quickstart

The test suite runs entirely against in-memory fakes in internal/fakes, which model Formance pagination and Blnk double-entry semantics (duplicate references, atomic bulk rollback, lost responses). When you change behaviour, add a scenario to migrator/migrator_test.go.

docs.title: Guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep the module dependency-free (standard library only) unless there is a compelling reason.
  • Money is always amount.Amount — never float64.
  • Every write to Blnk must carry a deterministic reference.
  • Public APIs need doc comments; user-visible changes need a docs update and a CHANGELOG.md entry.
  • Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (feat:, fix:, docs: …).

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: Tag vX.Y.Z on main. The release workflow builds binaries and multi-arch container images with GoReleaser. make release-check validates .goreleaser.yaml and make snapshot builds a local release without publishing.

docs.title: Cutover runbook
docs.text: A checklist for moving production traffic from Formance to Blnk with minimal downtime, using replay's incremental catch-up. The -volumes checks assume the default reverts: replay; with reverts: skip, use plain reconcile (see Reconciliation).

docs.title: Rehearse in staging
docs.text:
• Restore a recent copy of Formance data (or use a read replica) and a fresh Blnk instance.
  • formance2blnk validate and formance2blnk plan — review ledgers, balance counts and every skip reason.
  • formance2blnk migrate — note throughput (tx_per_sec in logs) to estimate production duration.
  • formance2blnk reconcile -volumes returns 0.
  • Interrupt a run with Ctrl-C and re-run it; confirm it resumes and reconciliation still passes.
  • Spot-check a few Blnk transactions against Formance (meta_data.formance_tx_id).

docs.title: Bulk migration (Formance still live)
docs.text:
• Point the config at production; use a new state file.
  • Set requests_per_second on the Formance side if you need to protect it.
  • formance2blnk migrate — this may take hours for large ledgers; it can be stopped and resumed at any time.

docs.title: Cutover window
docs.text:
• Freeze writes to Formance (maintenance mode / feature flag).
  • formance2blnk migrate — catch-up processes only the transactions since the last run, usually seconds.
  • formance2blnk reconcile -volumes -format json -out cutover-report.json returns 0.
  • Switch application writes to Blnk.
  • Unfreeze.

docs.title: Afterwards
docs.text:
• Archive the state file and the reconciliation report with your change record.
  • Keep Formance read-only for an agreed period.
  • Don't run migrate again once Blnk receives live traffic.

Snapshot or hybrid cutovers

Snapshot has no incremental catch-up, so run it inside the freeze window. For hybrid, run the snapshot and most of the replay beforehand, then a final migrate (which only replays new transactions) during the freeze.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: All examples live in the examples/ directory and are built in CI; the quickstart and custom-mapper examples are also run there.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
A complete replay and reconciliation against in-memory fakes — no servers required.

go run ./examples/quickstart

Replayed 5 Formance transactions into 7 Blnk transactions (2 ledgers, 3 balances)
Reconciliation: ok=true checked=5 matched=5
Second run wrote 0 transactions

// Quickstart runs a complete migration against in-memory fakes of Formance
// and Blnk, so you can see the whole flow without any servers:
//
//  go run ./examples/quickstart
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log/slog"
    "os"
    "time"

    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/blnk"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/formance"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/internal/fakes"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/mapping"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/migrator"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/state"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    fm, bk := fakes.NewFormance(), fakes.NewBlnk()
    defer fm.Close()
    defer bk.Close()

    // 1. A small Formance history: deposits, a payment with a fee, a
    //    refund (revert) and a withdrawal.
    t0 := time.Date(2025, 1, 1, 9, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
    post := func(h int, ps ...formance.Posting) uint64 {
        return fm.Post("main", t0.Add(time.Duration(h)*time.Hour), ps, map[string]string{"description": "demo"})
    }
    usd := func(src, dst string, v int64) formance.Posting {
        return formance.Posting{Source: src, Destination: dst, Amount: fakes.Amt(v), Asset: "USD/2"}
    }
    post(0, usd("world", "users:alice:wallet", 50_00))
    post(1, usd("world", "users:bob:wallet", 20_00))
    pay := post(2, usd("users:alice:wallet", "merchants:acme:main", 12_50), usd("users:alice:wallet", "platform:fees", 50))
    fm.Revert("main", pay, t0.Add(3*time.Hour))
    post(4, usd("users:bob:wallet", "world", 5_00))

    // 2. Wire up clients, mapping and a state store.
    src, _ := formance.New(formance.Options{BaseURL: fm.URL()})
    dst, _ := blnk.New(blnk.Options{BaseURL: bk.URL()})
    mapper, err := mapping.New(mapping.Config{Rules: []mapping.Rule{
        {Match: "platform:fees", Indicator: "@Fees"},
        {Match: "users:*:wallet", Ledger: "Customer Wallets"},
        {Match: "merchants:**", Ledger: "Merchants"},
    }})
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    m, err := migrator.New(src, dst, migrator.Options{
        Ledgers: []string{"main"},
        Mapper:  mapper,
        Store:   state.NewMemory(),
        Logger:  slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(os.Stderr, &slog.HandlerOptions{Level: slog.LevelWarn})),
    })
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    // 3. Plan-free replay, then reconcile.
    st, err := m.Replay(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("Replayed %d Formance transactions into %d Blnk transactions (%d ledgers, %d balances)\n",
        st.FormanceTxs, st.BlnkTxs, st.LedgersCreated, st.BalancesCreated)

    rep, err := m.Reconcile(ctx, migrator.ReconcileOptions{CheckVolumes: true})
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("Reconciliation: ok=%v checked=%d matched=%d\n", rep.OK(), rep.Checked, rep.Matched)

    // 4. Re-running is safe: nothing is written twice.
    again, _ := m.Replay(ctx)
    fmt.Printf("Second run wrote %d transactions\n", again.BlnkTxs)
}

docs.title: Production
docs.text:
Embedding the migrator in your own program: OAuth2 against Formance Cloud, a durable state file, graceful shutdown, structured logs, a progress callback and a strict reconciliation gate.

// Production shows how to embed the migrator in your own program against
// real servers, with a durable state file, graceful shutdown, a progress
// callback and a strict reconciliation gate.
//
//  FORMANCE_URL=https://ORG.ENV.formance.cloud/api/ledger \
//  FORMANCE_CLIENT_ID=... FORMANCE_CLIENT_SECRET=... \
//  BLNK_URL=https://blnk.internal BLNK_API_KEY=... \
//  go run ./examples/production -ledger main
package main

import (
    "context"
    "flag"
    "fmt"
    "log/slog"
    "os"
    "os/signal"
    "syscall"

    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/blnk"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/formance"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/mapping"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/migrator"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/state"
)

func main() {
    ledger := flag.String("ledger", "main", "Formance ledger to migrate")
    statePath := flag.String("state", "migration-state.json", "state file")
    flag.Parse()

    logger := slog.New(slog.NewJSONHandler(os.Stderr, nil))
    ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
    defer stop()

    if err := run(ctx, logger, *ledger, *statePath); err != nil {
        logger.Error("migration failed", "err", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
}

func run(ctx context.Context, logger *slog.Logger, ledger, statePath string) error {
    src, err := formance.New(formance.Options{
        BaseURL:           os.Getenv("FORMANCE_URL"),
        ClientID:          os.Getenv("FORMANCE_CLIENT_ID"),
        ClientSecret:      os.Getenv("FORMANCE_CLIENT_SECRET"),
        PageSize:          100,
        RequestsPerSecond: 20, // be gentle with the source
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    dst, err := blnk.New(blnk.Options{BaseURL: os.Getenv("BLNK_URL"), APIKey: os.Getenv("BLNK_API_KEY")})
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    mapper, err := mapping.New(mapping.Config{
        Rules: []mapping.Rule{
            {Match: "platform:fees", Indicator: "@Fees"},
            {Match: "platform:float:*", Indicator: "@Float-{1}"},
            {Match: "users:*:wallet", Ledger: "Customer Wallets"},
            {Match: "merchants:**", Ledger: "Merchants"},
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    store, err := state.OpenFile(statePath)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer store.Close() // flushes and releases the lock, also on Ctrl-C

    m, err := migrator.New(src, dst, migrator.Options{
        Ledgers:             []string{ledger},
        Mapper:              mapper,
        Store:               store,
        Logger:              logger,
        CopyAccountMetadata: true,
        Progress: func(s migrator.Stats) {
            logger.Info("progress", "ledger", s.Ledger, "formance_txs", s.FormanceTxs, "blnk_txs", s.BlnkTxs)
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    stats, err := m.Replay(ctx)
    logger.Info("replay finished", "stats", stats)
    if err != nil {
        return err // re-run the program to resume from the checkpoint
    }

    report, err := m.Reconcile(ctx, migrator.ReconcileOptions{CheckVolumes: true})
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if !report.OK() {
        for _, mm := range report.Mismatches {
            logger.Error("mismatch", "target", mm.Target, "accounts", mm.Accounts, "field", mm.Field,
                "expected", mm.Expected, "actual", mm.Actual)
        }
        return fmt.Errorf("%d reconciliation mismatches", len(report.Mismatches))
    }
    logger.Info("ledgers match", "checked", report.Checked)
    return nil
}

docs.title: Custom mapper
docs.text:
Implementing mapping.Mapper to route accounts to a Blnk ledger per country, falling back to the rules mapper.

// Custom-mapper shows how to plug your own account-routing logic into the
// migrator by implementing mapping.Mapper. Here, accounts are routed to a
// Blnk ledger per country taken from the address, and any asset ending in
// "_TEST" is mapped to a sandbox currency.
//
//  go run ./examples/custom-mapper
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "strings"
    "time"

    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/blnk"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/formance"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/internal/fakes"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/mapping"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/migrator"
)

// countryMapper routes "users:<country>:<id>" to "Wallets <COUNTRY>" and
// falls back to the rules mapper for everything else.
type countryMapper struct {
    fallback *mapping.Rules
}

func (c countryMapper) Account(ledger, address string) (mapping.Target, error) {
    parts := strings.Split(address, ":")
    if len(parts) == 3 && parts[0] == "users" {
        return mapping.Target{Kind: mapping.KindBalance, Ledger: "Wallets " + strings.ToUpper(parts[1])}, nil
    }
    return c.fallback.Account(ledger, address)
}

func (c countryMapper) Asset(asset string) (mapping.Asset, error) {
    a, err := c.fallback.Asset(asset)
    if err == nil && strings.HasSuffix(a.Currency, "_TEST") {
        a.Currency = "SANDBOX"
    }
    return a, err
}

func main() {
    fm, bk := fakes.NewFormance(), fakes.NewBlnk()
    defer fm.Close()
    defer bk.Close()
    now := time.Now()
    fm.Post("main", now, []formance.Posting{{Source: "world", Destination: "users:ng:1", Amount: fakes.Amt(500000), Asset: "NGN/2"}}, nil)
    fm.Post("main", now, []formance.Posting{{Source: "world", Destination: "users:gh:7", Amount: fakes.Amt(9000), Asset: "GHS/2"}}, nil)

    rules, _ := mapping.New(mapping.Config{})
    src, _ := formance.New(formance.Options{BaseURL: fm.URL()})
    dst, _ := blnk.New(blnk.Options{BaseURL: bk.URL()})
    m, err := migrator.New(src, dst, migrator.Options{Ledgers: []string{"main"}, Mapper: countryMapper{rules}})
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    st, err := m.Replay(context.Background())
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    fmt.Printf("created %d ledgers and %d balances\n", st.LedgersCreated, st.BalancesCreated)
}

docs.title: Configuration files
Migrate several Formance ledgers into one Blnk ledger
docs.text:
{
  "formance": { "url": "...", "ledgers": ["eu", "us"] },
  "mapping": { "default_ledger": "Customers" }
}

References include the Formance ledger name, so transactions from different ledgers never collide. Balances stay separate per Formance ledger.

docs.title: One Blnk ledger per account prefix
docs.text:
{
  "mapping": {
    "rules": [
      { "match": "world", "indicator": "@World" },
      { "match": "*:**",  "ledger": "{1}" }
    ]
  }
}

users:1:wallet → ledger users, merchants:9 → ledger merchants. The explicit world rule is needed because ** matches zero segments, so *:** would otherwise also catch world (rules are checked before the world_indicator default).

docs.title: Run in Docker with a mounted state directory
docs.text:
docker run --rm \
  -v "$PWD:/work" \
  -e BLNK_API_KEY \
  ghcr.io/otyang/formance2blnk:latest migrate -config /work/formance2blnk.json -state /work/state/state.json

docs.title: Gate a pipeline on reconciliation
docs.text:
formance2blnk migrate -log-format json
formance2blnk reconcile -volumes -format json -out report.json

reconcile exits with code 2 on any difference, failing the job.

docs.title: Re-run with one-at-a-time writes
docs.text: If your Blnk deployment does not support atomic bulk writes, set "migration": { "batch_size": 1 }. Each Formance posting is then sent individually (multi-posting Formance transactions lose atomicity across postings, but references keep re-runs safe).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
GoBinaryDockerFrom source 
go install github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/cmd/formance2blnk@latest

Download an archive for your platform from the releases page, extract it and put formance2blnk on your PATH.

docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/otyang/formance2blnk:latest help

git clone https://github.com/otyang/formance2blnk && cd formance2blnk
make build   # → bin/formance2blnk

Check it works:

formance2blnk version

docs.title: Try it without servers
docs.text:
The repository includes in-memory fakes of both APIs. This runs a full replay and reconciliation in a second:

go run ./examples/quickstart

Replayed 5 Formance transactions into 7 Blnk transactions (2 ledgers, 3 balances)
Reconciliation: ok=true checked=5 matched=5
Second run wrote 0 transactions

docs.title: 1. Create a configuration
docs.text:
formance2blnk init > formance2blnk.json

Edit the URLs, the list of Formance ledgers and the mapping rules. Secrets can come from the environment:

{
  "formance": { "url": "http://localhost:3068", "ledgers": ["main"], "token": "${FORMANCE_TOKEN:-}" },
  "blnk":     { "url": "http://localhost:5001", "api_key": "${BLNK_API_KEY:-}" },
  "mapping":  { "rules": [ { "match": "users:*:wallet", "ledger": "Customer Wallets" } ] },
  "migration": { "mode": "replay" }
}

docs.title: 2. Validate
docs.text:
formance2blnk validate

This checks required fields, unknown keys, mapping rule syntax and mode settings without contacting either server, and prints the configuration with secrets redacted.

docs.title: 3. Plan (dry run)
docs.text:
formance2blnk plan

plan reads everything from Formance and computes exactly what would be written — ledgers, balances, transactions and skipped postings — without writing to Blnk or the state file.

docs.title: 4. Migrate
docs.text:
formance2blnk migrate

Progress is logged periodically. If the run stops for any reason, run the same command again; it resumes from the checkpoint.

docs.title: 5. Reconcile
docs.text:
formance2blnk reconcile -volumes

Exit code 0 means every balance matches. See Reconciliation for what is compared.

Run against staging first

Point the tool at a staging Blnk instance and a copy (or read replica) of your Formance data, migrate, reconcile, and only then plan the production cutover.

docs.title: Go library
docs.text:
go get github.com/otyang/formance2blnk

The module has no third-party dependencies. API docs: pkg.go.dev.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package Purpose migrator The engine: Replay, ReplaySince, Snapshot, SnapshotAsOf, Hybrid, Reconcile. mapping Mapper interface and the rules-based implementation. formance Read-only Formance Ledger v2 client. blnk Blnk client: ledgers, balances, transactions, bulk. state Store interface; OpenFile (durable, locked) and NewMemory. config Load the CLI's JSON configuration and build clients/options from it. amount Arbitrary-precision amounts that round-trip through JSON.

docs.title: Minimal program
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "log"
    "os"

    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/blnk"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/formance"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/mapping"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/migrator"
    "github.com/otyang/formance2blnk/state"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    src, err := formance.New(formance.Options{BaseURL: "http://localhost:3068"})
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    dst, err := blnk.New(blnk.Options{BaseURL: "http://localhost:5001", APIKey: os.Getenv("BLNK_API_KEY")})
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    mapper, err := mapping.New(mapping.Config{Rules: []mapping.Rule{
        {Match: "users:*:wallet", Ledger: "Customer Wallets"},
    }})
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    store, err := state.OpenFile("state.json")
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    defer store.Close()

    m, err := migrator.New(src, dst, migrator.Options{
        Ledgers: []string{"main"},
        Mapper:  mapper,
        Store:   store,
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    if _, err := m.Replay(ctx); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    rep, err := m.Reconcile(ctx, migrator.ReconcileOptions{CheckVolumes: true})
    if err != nil || !rep.OK() {
        log.Fatalf("reconciliation failed: %v %+v", err, rep.Mismatches)
    }
}

docs.title: Reusing the CLI configuration
docs.text:
cfg, _ := config.Load("formance2blnk.json")
src, _ := cfg.FormanceClient()
dst, _ := cfg.BlnkClient()
opts, _ := cfg.MigratorOptions(slog.Default())
store, _ := cfg.OpenState()
defer store.Close()
opts.Store = store
m, _ := migrator.New(src, dst, opts)

docs.title: Transform
docs.text:
Edit or drop every Blnk transaction before it is sent:

opts.Transform = func(req *blnk.TransactionRequest, tx migrator.TxContext) (bool, error) {
    if tx.Transaction.Metadata["test"] == "true" {
        return false, nil // drop test traffic
    }
    req.Description = "Migrated: " + req.Description
    req.MetaData["migration_batch"] = "2026-10"
    return true, nil
}

TxContext gives the source ledger, the full Formance transaction, and the posting with its index. For snapshot opening balances, PostingIndex is -1, Transaction is empty and Posting is synthesised from the volume.

Warning

Don't change Reference, amounts, source or destination in a Transform unless you fully understand the consequences: references are what make re-runs safe, and the others affect reconciliation.

docs.title: Progress
docs.text:
opts.Progress = func(s migrator.Stats) {
    slog.Info("migration progress", "ledger", s.Ledger, "formance_txs", s.FormanceTxs, "blnk_txs", s.BlnkTxs)
}
opts.ProgressEvery = 5000

docs.title: Custom stores
docs.text: Implement state.Store to keep progress in Postgres, Redis or a cloud object store. The interface is small: ledger and balance ID lookups, a Balances listing, checkpoints per Formance ledger and phase, the transactions dropped under reverts: skip (MarkSkippedTx / SkippedTx), Flush and Close. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use and should make Put* and SetCheckpoint durable before returning. A MarkSkippedTx must be durable no later than the next SetCheckpoint.

docs.title: Custom sources and destinations
docs.text: migrator.New accepts any migrator.Source and migrator.Destination. Wrap the provided clients to add tracing, or substitute your own — for example a source that reads a Formance export file instead of the API.

docs.title: Mapping
docs.text: Mapping decides where each Formance account and asset lands in Blnk. It lives in the mapping section of the configuration.

docs.title: Targets
docs.text:
Each Formance account resolves to exactly one target:

Target Rule field Result in Blnk Balance "ledger": "Name" A regular balance in the named ledger, created on first use (one per asset). Indicator "indicator": "@Name" An internal balance addressed by indicator. Blnk creates it on first use. Skip "skip": true Not migrated. See on_skipped_account.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rules are evaluated in order; the first match wins. If nothing matches, world maps to world_indicator (default @World) and every other account maps to a balance in default_ledger (default {ledger}, the Formance ledger's own name). Rules are checked before the world default, so a rule that matches world (for example *:** or **) overrides world_indicator.

Each rule must set exactly one of ledger, indicator or skip, and a non-empty match. Indicators (including world_indicator) must start with @. Invalid rules are rejected when the mapper is created.

{
  "mapping": {
    "world_indicator": "@World",
    "default_ledger": "Formance {ledger}",
    "rules": [
      { "match": "platform:fees",    "indicator": "@Fees" },
      { "match": "banks:*",          "indicator": "@Bank-{1}" },
      { "match": "users:*:wallet",   "ledger": "Customer Wallets" },
      { "match": "merchants:**",     "ledger": "Merchants" },
      { "match": "sandbox:**",       "skip": true }
    ]
  }
}
Address Result world @World platform:fees @Fees banks:gtbank @Bank-gtbank users:42:wallet balance in Customer Wallets users:42:savings balance in Formance main merchants:9:pending:eur balance in Merchants sandbox:anything skipped

docs.title: Pattern syntax
docs.text:
Patterns match the :-separated address segment by segment.

Pattern Matches literal exactly that segment * any single segment user_*, acc-?? glob within one segment (path.Match syntax) ** zero or more trailing segments — only allowed as the last segment

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
ledger and indicator values may use:

Placeholder Value {ledger} the source Formance ledger name {0} the full address {1}, {2}, … the segments captured by wildcards, in order (a glob segment captures the whole segment; ** captures the :-joined remainder, possibly empty)

Unknown placeholders are left unchanged.

docs.title: Skipped accounts
docs.text:
on_skipped_account controls postings that touch a skipped account:

  • error (default) — stop the migration. Safe: you notice before balances diverge.
  • drop — drop the posting and count it under skipped_account. The counter-party's balance in Blnk will differ from Formance by those postings.

In snapshot mode, a skipped account with a non-zero balance is an error unless the policy is drop.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
Formance assets are CODE or CODE/DECIMALS (the code starts with a letter and may contain letters, digits and _; at most 30 decimals). They become a Blnk currency and a precision multiplier of 10^DECIMALS:

Formance Blnk currency Precision USD/2 USD 100 BTC/8 BTC 100000000 JPY JPY 1

Override per asset, keyed by the full Formance asset (USD/2, COIN); decimals also changes the precision:

{ "mapping": { "assets": { "COIN": { "currency": "NGN", "decimals": 2 } } } }

docs.title: Custom mappers (Go)
docs.text:
In the library, anything implementing mapping.Mapper can be passed as Options.Mapper:

type Mapper interface {
    Account(sourceLedger, address string) (Target, error)
    Asset(asset string) (Asset, error)
}

See examples/custom-mapper for a mapper that routes accounts to a ledger per country and falls back to the rules mapper.

Mappings must be stable

Don't change mapping rules between runs of the same migration. Existing balances are looked up in the state file by Formance ledger, address and asset, so an account that already has a Blnk balance keeps it as long as it still maps to a balance (even if the rule now names another ledger). Indicator and skip targets are not stored, so changes to them take effect immediately, splitting the account's history.

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text:
reconcile reads current volumes from Formance and compares them with Blnk balances.

formance2blnk reconcile                  # net balances
formance2blnk reconcile -volumes         # + credit/debit volumes (after a full replay)
formance2blnk reconcile -format csv -out drift.csv

With -out, the report goes to the file and a one-line summary is printed to stdout. -workers (default 8) sets the number of concurrent Blnk balance lookups.

docs.title: What is compared
docs.text:
For each (Formance ledger, account, asset):

Mapped to Compared against A balance The Blnk balance recorded in the state file for that account and asset. An indicator The Blnk indicator balance for that currency. Several Formance accounts mapped to the same indicator — including across ledgers — are summed. An indicator that does not exist in Blnk counts as zero. Skip Not compared (counted as skipped). Indicators are skipped too with -skip-indicators. Field Formance Blnk balance balance balance credit_balance (with -volumes) input credit_balance debit_balance (with -volumes) output debit_balance

A Formance account mapped to a balance but with no Blnk balance in the state file is reported with field missing if its balance (or, with -volumes, its input/output) is non-zero; otherwise it is counted as skipped. A failed Blnk lookup is reported with field error.

docs.title: When to use -volumes
docs.text:
Volume checks only hold after a full replay with reverts: replay. Snapshot, hybrid and reverts: skip produce the same net balances but different credit/debit totals, so use net-balance reconciliation for those.

Formance postings from an account to itself — or between two accounts mapped to the same Blnk balance or indicator — are skipped (Blnk rejects them); they add equally to Formance input and output, so they can show up as volume differences but never as balance differences.

docs.text:

bln_0a1b2c,main:users:2:wallet (USD/2),balance,15000,14700,difference -300

docs.title: Exit codes
Common causes of drift
docs.text:
• Writes to Formance after the last migrate run — run migrate again (replay catches up incrementally).
  • Writes to Blnk outside the migration — reconcile before opening Blnk to traffic.
  • Changed mapping rules between runs.
  • Dropped postings with on_skipped_account: drop or a Transform that returns keep=false.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
Choose a strategy with migration.mode (or -mode on the command line).

Replay Snapshot Hybrid Transaction history in Blnk Full None After the cutoff Blnk transactions written One per posting One per non-zero (account, asset) Both Speed Slowest Fastest In between Credit/debit volumes match Formance Yes No No Net balances match Formance Yes Yes Yes Incremental catch-up Yes — Yes Typical use Regulated / audit-heavy Fresh start Long history, recent detail

docs.title: Replay
docs.text:
{ "migration": { "mode": "replay" } }

Every Formance transaction is re-recorded in Blnk in ID order with its original timestamp as effective_date. Blnk ends up with the same history, the same balances and the same credit/debit volumes as Formance (verify with reconcile -volumes).

Replay is incremental: running it again only processes transactions created since the last checkpoint. That makes it ideal for a near-zero-downtime cutover — migrate while Formance is live, then run one short catch-up after freezing writes.

docs.title: Reverts
docs.text:
Formance reverts a transaction by recording a new transaction with the opposite postings and the metadata key com.formance.spec/state/reverts; the original is flagged reverted.

  • reverts: replay (default) — both the original and the revert are replayed. History mirrors Formance exactly.
  • reverts: skip — reverted transactions and their reverts are both dropped. Net balances still match; credit/debit volumes will not.

With reverts: skip, a transaction is dropped only if it is already reverted when the migrator reads it, and the migrator records each one it drops in the state file. A revert is dropped only if its original was. If the original was migrated before it was reverted, for example in an earlier run followed by an incremental catch-up, the revert is replayed so Blnk stays in balance. A revert that is itself reverted is handled the same way.

docs.title: Snapshot
docs.text:
{ "migration": { "mode": "snapshot" } }

For each Formance ledger, the migrator reads volumes for every (account, asset) and writes one opening-balance transaction per non-zero balance:

  • positive balance: @World → balance
  • negative balance: balance → @World

Opening balances are dated at the time of the run. The counter-party is the mapped world indicator by default, which makes the Blnk @World balance equal to Formance's world account. Use opening_indicator to use a dedicated equity balance (e.g. @OpeningBalances) instead.

The world account itself is skipped (it is the counter-party). An account mapped to skip that holds a non-zero balance aborts the snapshot unless on_skipped_account is drop. Set include_zero_balances: true to also create Blnk balances for accounts (mapped to a balance, not an indicator) whose balance is zero, so every such account exists in Blnk.

Each completed ledger is marked in the state file; running the snapshot again skips it. An interrupted snapshot is simply re-run: opening balances already written are recognised by their deterministic reference.

docs.title: Hybrid
docs.text:
{ "migration": { "mode": "hybrid", "cutoff": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" } }
  1. Snapshot as of the cutoff — balances from transactions effective strictly before cutoff (Formance volumes with endTime).
  2. Replay from the cutoff — every transaction effective at or after cutoff, in ID order. Earlier transactions are still read from Formance but skipped (before_cutoff).

Opening balances are dated at the cutoff, so Blnk's history begins there. With reverts: skip, a revert of a pre-cutoff transaction is still replayed, because the original is inside the snapshot and was never dropped.

Cutoff semantics

The cutoff applies to the effective timestamp, which is what Formance volumes use with endTime. Backdated transactions inserted after the cutoff but effective before it are part of the snapshot only if they exist when the snapshot runs; ones inserted later are skipped by the replay (before_cutoff) and show up as drift. Always finish with a reconciliation.

The cutoff must not be in the future, and it is recorded in the state file once the snapshot completes: re-running with a different cutoff against the same state file is refused, because it would double-count or drop the transactions between the two cutoffs.

docs.title: Choosing
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  A{Need full transaction history in Blnk?} -->|Yes| R[Replay]
  A -->|No| B{Need recent history?}
  B -->|Yes| H[Hybrid with a cutoff]
  B -->|No| S[Snapshot]

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
state: file is locked by another run

Another migrator is using the same state file, or a previous run was killed with SIGKILL. Check no other process is running, then delete the <state_file>.lock file next to the state file (the error names it).

account "x" is mapped to skip

A posting touches an account your rules skip. Either change the rule or set on_skipped_account: drop if dropping those postings is intended.

mapping: invalid asset

Asset names must be CODE or CODE/DECIMALS: a letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, with at most 30 decimals. Names that don't fit cannot be migrated with the built-in mapper; mapping.assets only changes the Blnk currency and decimals of valid assets. Use a custom mapping.Mapper through the library instead.

already completed with a different as-of time (cutoff)

A hybrid run's snapshot finished with one cutoff and you re-ran it with another. Resuming would double-count or drop the transactions between the two cutoffs, so it is refused. Re-run with the original cutoff, or start again with a new state file against an empty Blnk instance.

page has more results but no next cursor

The Formance server reported more pages but gave no cursor, or returned the same cursor twice. The migrator stops rather than checkpoint past transactions it never read. Check the Formance version and any proxy in between; see Compatibility.

Transactions rejected for insufficient funds

You set enforce_balances: true, and Formance allowed an overdraft that Blnk refuses. Remove the option (the default trusts Formance's validated history) or configure overdraft rules in Blnk.

A re-run reports Already migrated (skipped)

Expected after an interruption: those writes reached Blnk before the checkpoint was saved, and their references were recognised. Nothing was written twice.

Duplicates are not recognised on resume

Your Blnk version may word its duplicate-reference error differently. Run with -log-level debug to see the exact message and open an issue; the detection lives in blnk.IsDuplicateReference.

Reconciliation shows credit/debit differences but balances match

You used snapshot, hybrid or reverts: skip, or the ledger contains self-transfers. Run reconcile without -volumes. See Reconciliation.

Formance responds 429 or 5xx

Requests are retried automatically with exponential backoff (honouring Retry-After). Lower formance.requests_per_second to reduce load.

How do I start over?

Point the config at a fresh Blnk instance and delete the state file. To keep the same Blnk instance, also change reference_prefix, otherwise every write is recognised as already migrated.

docs.title: Why formance2blnk
docs.text: formance2blnk was built to move one line of business out of a shared Formance ledger and into its own Blnk instance, without losing a single unit of history along the way.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
A single Formance deployment held both fiat and crypto transactions. That caused two problems:

  • Shared blast radius. A spike in crypto activity competes with core banking for the same ledger and database. Heavy trading volume could slow the fiat rails, or lock them up entirely.
  • Regulatory exposure. Regulators increasingly expect fiat and digital-asset activity to be kept apart. Holding both in one ledger widens the audit scope and pulls the fiat rails into crypto-related scrutiny.

docs.title: The aim
docs.text: Separate the two businesses completely: no shared ledger, no shared infrastructure. Fiat stays on Formance. Crypto, including all of its historical ledger data, moves to a dedicated, standalone environment.

docs.title: The solution
docs.text:
The crypto business moves to Blnk. A data pipeline extracts the crypto accounts and their history from Formance and writes them into a standalone Blnk instance sized for that workload alone. Each side then scales, deploys and gets audited on its own terms.

That pipeline is formance2blnk. A migration like this has to meet a few non-negotiable requirements, and each one maps to a feature:

Requirement How formance2blnk meets it Move only the crypto side Mapping rules route crypto addresses into Blnk and skip everything else. Never lose or double-count value Exact integer amounts (BTC/8, ETH/18, …), deterministic references and idempotent writes. See Concepts. Keep the audit trail, or start clean Full history replay, an opening-balance snapshot, or a hybrid of the two. Survive a long-running pipeline Checkpointed and resumable: interrupt it and run the same command again. Prove the split is correct Reconciliation compares every migrated balance and exits non-zero on drift, ready for a cutover gate.

docs.title: Carving crypto out of a shared ledger
docs.text:
Skip rules match on the account address, so the carve-out works best when crypto accounts share an address prefix. In this example that prefix is crypto::

{
  "mapping": {
    "rules": [
      { "match": "world", "indicator": "@World" },
      { "match": "fiat:settlement:crypto", "indicator": "@FiatSettlement" },
      { "match": "crypto:users:*:wallet", "ledger": "Crypto Wallets" },
      { "match": "crypto:treasury", "indicator": "@CryptoTreasury" },
      { "match": "crypto:**", "ledger": "Crypto Operations" },
      { "match": "**", "skip": true }
    ]
  },
  "migration": { "on_skipped_account": "error" }
}

Three details matter:

  1. Map world before the catch-all. Rules are checked before the built-in world default, so without its own rule world would match ** and be skipped.
  2. Give cross-rail flows a boundary account. A transaction that moves value between a crypto account and a fiat account, such as a fiat on-ramp, touches both sides. Map the fiat side of those flows to an indicator like @FiatSettlement so the crypto balances stay complete in Blnk.
  3. Keep on_skipped_account: error for the first run. Any remaining transaction that crosses into a skipped (fiat) account aborts the run and names the account. You can then map it, or knowingly switch to drop. With drop, the crypto counter-party's balance in Blnk will differ from Formance by the dropped postings.

If crypto and fiat can't be told apart by address, for example one account holding both USD/2 and BTC/8, use the Go library's Transform hook to drop postings by asset:

opts.Transform = func(req *blnk.TransactionRequest, tx migrator.TxContext) (bool, error) {
    return !strings.HasPrefix(tx.Posting.Asset, "USD/"), nil // keep crypto only
}

Reconciliation still compares every asset on each migrated account. Fiat balances left behind on those accounts will therefore show up as differences, so filter or review them in the report.

docs.title: Is this your situation?
docs.text: The same approach works for any split, not only fiat and crypto: carving out a product line, a region, or a legal entity, or moving off Formance entirely. If you need to move ledger data from Formance to Blnk and prove afterwards that nothing changed, start with Getting started.
